dimensions.assessment: Affects certain nonprimary commercial service airports with 2,500 to 10,000 annual passenger boardings serving aircraft under 60,000 pounds.
dimensions.evidence: For certain nonprimary commercial service airports (i.e., airports that have 2,500 to 10,000 passenger boardings annually) that serve aircraft that do not exceed 60,000 pounds gross weight

dimensions.assessment: Relates to procedural allowances for using state highway standards instead of federal standards on specific pavement projects.
dimensions.evidence: reduces the requirements for the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to allow a state to use its state highway standards, instead of federal standards, for airfield pavement projects

dimensions.assessment: No significant federal spending or revenue implications are stated beyond administrative processes for existing program funds.
Amends title 49 of the United States Code regarding airfield pavement construction standards and FAA determination timelines.
dimensions.evidence: To amend title 49, United States Code, to permit the use of State highway standards for airfield pavement construction and improvement under certain circumstances

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory amendment governing ongoing FAA project approvals.

missing_information: Exact number of airports nationwide that meet the specific weight and passenger criteria.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill makes administrative changes to requirements for certain smaller commercial aviation airports regarding airfield pavement projects, affecting nonprimary airports with limited passenger boardings.
